description: Before adding a global library, ask whether the state is remote, URL, form or really UI state. Each kind has its own home.
The single owner of a value. Remote data is owned by the server; the client only caches it. A second copy needs syncing and drifts.
Explicit states and allowed transitions for a multi-step flow (checkout, upload, wizard), so impossible combinations cannot be represented.
GraphQL clients (Apollo, Relay) store entities by type and id, so an updated entity refreshes every query that includes it without invalidation.
An architecture artifact listing every piece of state with its kind, its home and the reason. Exposes duplicates and guides promotion decisions.
